analysis:
Examined all five changed files. None touch the provider runtime, the coordinator-to-provider wire, attestation or cache code, so the threat-model assets A-001 to A-010 and A-014 to A-020 are unaffected. The changes sit in CI and release tooling and bear on A-011/A-017 only indirectly.

1) scripts/ci-tested-tree.py: adds tree-keyed skip records (ci-tested-tree-<tree>-pcm). The reused-record source is still restricted to a completed, successful run of the same workflow path in the same repo, with head_repository equal to repository. Any API error runs the tests. The head binding is dropped for tree records, which gives the low finding above (a forged artifact from a modified same-repo PR workflow). The tree-name subcommand is benign.

2) scripts/provider_release_resume/api.py and scripts/resolve-provider-release.sh: workflow_dispatch on refs/heads/dev can now sign and publish a dev release. Gates: RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT must be dev, the commit must be GitHub-verified and on dev ancestry, and for dispatch the source must equal the current dev head. The shell forces validation_only=false and clears RELEASE_VERSION_OVERRIDE, and the staging and prod environments are rejected on this path. This adds no capability beyond a dev push by someone with write access, because the same lane already existed. Two minor points: a dispatch with validation_only=true on dev now publishes instead of failing, and the error text still says "push". The RELEASE_RESUME_RUN_ID early exec in resolve-provider-release.sh runs before these checks, and scripts/provider-release-resume.py is not supplied. The unreviewed question is whether a resume dispatched from dev reaches verify_workflow_source.

3) scripts/test-ci-component-paths.py is tests only. It encodes label-gated pull_request CI (run-ci and run-gpu-ci, with an unlabel job), path-filtered PRs into master, and removal of ci-dev-hourly. The workflow YAML files (ci-dev.yml, ci-master.yml, provider-plan.yml, provider-tests.yml) are not in this batch. Token permissions, who can apply labels, fork-PR handling and where the record artifact is uploaded are therefore unverified. These need integration review.

findings.detail: For a one-parent (squash) push, candidates() now adds a ("tree", None, None, ...) candidate. With record_head=None, tested_run() accepts any successful run of the same workflow file whose head_sha is merely a valid 40-hex SHA, from pull_request or push, whose artifact is named ci-tested-tree-<tree>-<flags>. Previously a record had to match the exact PR head, or the merge commit's actual parents. A same-repo PR runs its own, possibly modified, workflow, so a branch writer can make that workflow upload an empty ci-tested-tree-<T>-p1c1m1 artifact for a predicted tree T and finish green without running tests. If T later lands by squash merge (for example another PR's reviewed content on the current base), the push run skips its tests on the strength of that forged record. The docstring at lines 33-35 says the tree hash makes the record trustworthy, but the artifact name is not bound to what the producing run tested. Fix: require the producing run's head tree to equal T, or have the producer's own commit/tree checked via the API. Alternatively, restrict tree records to push runs of protected branches.
findings.title: Tree-keyed CI records drop the head/base binding, so a same-repo PR run can vouch for another change's tree
